title: Public API Load Hedging Scenarios — Q4 2026
body:
Purpose:
This sheet captures hedging (safety/backup) scenarios for the public-facing API peak windows projected for Q4 2026. Goal: recommend headroom targets in tokens/sec and QPS by region and GPU family, with clear provisioning guidance (reserved GPUs / on-demand buffer) and operational runbooks for activation.

High-level assumptions:
- Baseline traffic (median) estimated from 2026H1 trends + marketing forecast: +28% q/q into Q4.
- Peak behaviour: 95th percentile sustained for 10–30m bursts; 99th percentile spikes up to 3x 95p for <5m.
- Average token length per request: 220 tokens (chat-heavy day); embedding jobs separate.
- Typical model mix during peak: 40% LLM-small (L4-32GB), 45% LLM-medium (A100-40GB quantized), 15% LLM-large (H100-80GB full).
- Target average GPU utilization for serving pools: 60–70% during business-as-usual, 80% short-term acceptable during controlled bursts.

Summary table (projected peak windows, aggregated):
Region | Peak QPS (95p sustained 10m) | Peak tokens/sec (95p) | Peak QPS (99p spike) | Peak tokens/sec (99p) | Recommended headroom multiplier | Headroom tokens/sec target
US-WEST | 5,200 | 1,144,000 | 12,000 | 2,640,000 | 1.25 (buffer) + fallback | 3,300,000
US-EAST | 4,600 | 1,012,000 | 10,800 | 2,376,000 | 1.25 | 2,970,000
EU-WEST | 3,100 | 682,000 | 7,200 | 1,584,000 | 1.35 (latency slack) | 2,140,000
AP-SOUTH | 1,400 | 308,000 | 3,200 | 704,000 | 1.5 (capacity scarcity) | 1,056,000

Notes on multipliers: multipliers produce operational headroom that accounts for measurement error, placement fragmentation, and short-notice growth. For AP regions we recommend slightly higher multiplier due to sparser spare capacity and longer provisioning lead times.

GPU provisioning guidance (recommended mix to meet headroom tokens/sec targets):
- Mapping assumptions (average sustained tokens/sec per GPU under target model mix and batching):
  - H100-80GB: 90k tokens/sec (mixed batch, large model fraction)
  - A100-40GB: 48k tokens/sec (quantized medium models)
  - L4-32GB: 22k tokens/sec (small/fast models & embeddings offload)

Calculated reserve (rounded up to whole GPUs):
Region: US-WEST (headroom 3,300,000 tokens/sec) -> H100 need if all H100: 37; recommended mixed pool: 6 H100 + 40 A100 + 50 L4 (approx total equivalent capacity 3.35M tokens/sec).
Region: US-EAST -> recommend 5 H100 + 36 A100 + 40 L4 -> equivalent ~3.0M tokens/sec.
Region: EU-WEST -> recommend 3 H100 + 22 A100 + 30 L4 -> equivalent ~2.2M tokens/sec.
Region: AP-SOUTH -> recommend 1 H100 + 8 A100 + 15 L4 -> equivalent ~1.08M tokens/sec.

Operational playbook (activation thresholds and steps):
- Alerting: trigger when 95p sustained tokens/sec > 85% of non-reserved capacity for >5 minutes.
- Immediate actions (SRE on-call):
  1) Engage warm pool: scale dedicated GPU slices from reserved pool (pre-provisioned) — target bring-up time 90s.
  2) Enable aggressive batching/kv-cache-late-eviction policy (config: batch_target_ms +30%).
  3) Apply model downgrade routing for low-tier plans (fall back LLM-medium -> LLM-small for non-critical requests).
  4) If still above 98% capacity, flip regional fallback to adjacent region (US-WEST -> US-EAST) with routing cohort control.
- Post-incident: capture sample logs, annotate convo IDs for eval; run regression evals for quality drift due to downgrades.

Cost trade-offs and recommended reserved contracts:
- For predictable headroom we recommend converting 60% of headroom GPU requirements into Dedicated reserved capacity (1yr) with burstable on-demand allowance for 40%. This balances unit-cost with flexibility.
- Example delta over on-demand: reserved A100 ~ -28% unit cost; H100 reserved ~ -20% (numbers approximate; engage finance for firm quotes).

Runway and sensitivity scenarios (fast-check):
- Sensitivity A (marketing spike +50% vs baseline): headroom tokens/sec multiplies x1.5; immediate action: increase burst pool cap to 1.5x and move critical customers to dedicated lanes.
- Sensitivity B (regional outage US-EAST): reroute 60% traffic to US-WEST; increase US-WEST headroom by 1.4x; pre-warm spare H100s in US-WEST.
- Sensitivity C (sudden model shift to longer context average +40% tokens): tokens/sec increases proportionally; recommend immediate throttle on long-context experiments and reduce max_tokens in API for guest tier.

Open questions / risks:
- Actual peak token distribution per tenant unknown; tenant-level hot clusters could cause localized KV cache pressure and reduce per-GPU throughput by 8–12% (needs microbench).
- Placement fragmentation: the conservative multiplier may be insufficient if fragmentation persists; scheduling team to provide fragmentation loss estimates by next week (INF-3872).
- Spot vs on-demand mix in AP region not finalized; risk: sudden price/availability churn during global peaks.

Action items (owners & tentative dates):
- Run targeted bench (per-tenant KV cache pressure) across model mix: owner Amit Gupta, due 2026-10-20.
- Validate GPU token/sec mapping with live A/B (dark traffic): owner Sofia Alvarez, due 2026-10-25.
- Prepare dedicated-reserve purchase recommendation and cost model: owner Lucas Park + Finance, due 2026-11-08.
- Update routing playbook with safe-fallback cohort percentages: owner Maya Chen, due 2026-11-01.

Appendix (raw numbers used for quick checks):
- Day baseline median QPS (global aggregated): 28,000 QPS; tokens/sec baseline: 6.16M tokens/sec.
- Expected Q4 peak factor (marketing + product release cohort): 2.2x baseline for 95p sustained windows.
- Batch efficiency assumptions: 1.15x improvement for L4 at 25ms batching; 1.9x improvement for A100 at 40ms batches; H100 strong scaling but sensitive to long tail.

References: confluence INF-2043 capacity model, JIRA INF-3872 (bench), PR #212 infra-provisioning for burst pools.

Comments / notes to self (rough):
- Keep AP headroom fat; swapping to remote regions has nonlinear latency effects.
- We should simulate a 3-region failover in the infra chaos repo next sprint.
- Need a short customer comms play for rate-limited tiers — draft with CS once reserve sizing final.

---
Document version: working sheet v0.3 (iterative)
